entities.summary: García Álvarez de Toledo, 4th Marquis of Villafranca, was a Spanish general and politician born on September 8, 1514, in Villafranca del Bierzo, Spain, and died on June 10, 1577. As the Marquess of Villafranca, he played a crucial role in the Reconquista, leading the Spanish army to victory in the Battle of Lepanto in 1571. His military campaigns against the Ottoman Empire and his role in the Spanish conquest of North Africa contributed to the expansion of Spanish influence in the region. García Álvarez de Toledo's legacy extends beyond his military victories, as he also served as a diplomat and advisor to King Philip II, playing a key role in shaping Spanish foreign policy during the late 16th century. The Marquess's impact on Spanish history is a testament to his strategic thinking and leadership abilities, cementing his place as one of the most influential figures of the Spanish Golden Age.
